def find_longest_repeating_subseq(s):
    n = len(s)
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    
    # dp[i][j] stores the length of the longest common subsequence 
    # between s[:i] and s[:j].
    dp = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, n + 1):
            if s[i-1] == s[j-1]:
                # Characters match. We can either:
                # 1. Extend the subsequence from the previous match.
                # 2. Skip one character to ensure the two subsequences 
                #    do not share the same string characters at the same positions.
                dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]
            else:
                # Characters do not match. We must skip at least one 
                # position in one of the subsequences to avoid identical 
                # placement of characters.
                dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1])
    
    return dp[n][n]

    # Start with a large gap and reduce it
    gap = n // 2
    while gap > 0:
        for i in range(gap, n):
            # Move the element 'gap' positions ahead
            temp = arr[i]
            # Insert the element into the sorted part of the array
            j = i - gap
            while j >= 0 and arr[j] > temp:

    if p == 1:
        return 0
    if p <= n:
        return 0
    # Compute nCr modulo p using Lucas theorem
    res = 1
    while n > 0:

        ri = r % p
        if ni >= ri:
            # Compute ni choose ri modulo p
            num = 1
            den = 1
            for i in range(ri):
                num = num * (ni - i) % p
                den = den * (ri - i) % p
            res = res * num % p * pow(den, p - 2, p) % p
        n //= p
        r //= p
    return res

    bin_y = bin(y)[2:]

    bin_x = bin_x.zfill(max_len)
    bin_y = bin_y.zfill(max_len)
